name: Ahisamach
overview: Ahisamach is a male member of the tribe of Dan, noted in Scripture primarily as the father of Oholiab. His mention is brief but significant in the context of the skilled craftsmanship associated with his son. No additional personal details or notes are provided beyond his tribal affiliation and paternal role.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahisamach means '[my] brother is a support,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with a potentially encouraging or relational significance. This name is not indicated as being given directly by God, but it carries a meaningful expression in its original language.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ahisamach as a descendant of the tribe of Dan and as the father of Oholiab. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are documented in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Ahisamach's significance in the biblical narrative is primarily through his son, Oholiab, whom God appointed to assist in the artistic and skilled work for the tabernacle. His tribal identity as a Danite situates him within the broader covenant community of Israel. Though Ahisamach himself is not described as a craftsman, his role as father to a key artisan links him to the divine work of tabernacle construction.
